_comment:
House drafting standard. One file, reused for every job -- the job itself is an intake workbook, not a config.

The difference from sld_config*.json: those name an absolute sheet elevation for every device, so a cubicle that lacks a device needs a whole new archetype at new elevations. That is why 'two CTs' ended up baked into type NAMES, and why two-high decks are blocked. Here a device declares only its gap from the device above it, and the builder stacks whatever the intake row actually calls for.

A device is drawn if and only if its 'when' column has a value in the unit row. No archetype inherits a device from a drawing it was copied from.

sheet._pitch_note: All units drawn to the widest, per IOM practice. Overridden by --pitch.
sheet._frame_note: Symmetric about the bus: 9.148 of cubicle each side, so a two-high cubicle gives both decks the same room and the bus lands at the mid level. The lower deck takes its cable out through the floor, the upper deck out through the roof, exactly as each other's mirror image.
sheet._bus_label_note: Filled from the Project tab rather than fixed in the config, so the bus label can never disagree with the job it was drawn for.

_stack_note: Ordered top to bottom. 'gap' is the drop from the previous PRESENT device's anchor to this one's, so a skipped device closes the stack up rather than leaving a hole. Gaps measured off sld_config_assignment.json, which reproduces them exactly when every device is present.

stack.name: drawout_upper
stack._gap_note: From bus_y down to the upper primary disconnect.
stack._when_note: The primary disconnects are the breaker's own drawout contacts, so they come and go with it. A deck holding only a bus PT has no breaker to rack out.

stack.name: breaker
stack._when_note: A cubicle without a breaker rating has no breaker. That is what lets a deck hold only a bus PT.

stack.name: drawout_lower
stack._when_note: The primary disconnects are the breaker's own drawout contacts, so they come and go with it. A deck holding only a bus PT has no breaker to rack out.

stack.name: ct_protection
stack._secondary_note: Out of the CT's upper secondary terminal to 0.966, then up into the bottom edge of its own relay box. dy 0.249 and dx_from 0.224 are the terminal itself, read off the VXF1CT block; 0.966 is the offset 8508 uses on a feeder. So a generated feeder's secondary starts on the terminal and lands where a draughtsman would have put it.

stack.name: ct_differential
stack._secondary_note: This core does not go to its own relay -- it goes to the differential relay, which lives in another cubicle. So it leaves the LOWER terminal, steps out to 1.789 (8508's offset for a CT secondary that leaves the unit) and rises onto the lineup-wide bus_differential run instead of into the relay box above it. Taking the other terminal from ct_protection is what keeps the two leads from running one on top of the other where the CTs are close.
stack._note: The second core of the feeder CT, brought out as its own symbol because it feeds a different circuit -- bus differential on a feeder, the far bus's differential on a tie. A dual-core CT (1200/5/5A 5P20/5P20) is one piece of iron in the panel schedule and two symbols on the single line, which is why this is a separate row here rather than a wider label on ct_protection.

stack.name: ct_metering
stack._secondary_note: A metering CT's secondary does not go to a relay -- it goes to a test switch, so a technician can short the CT and inject current without pulling the panel apart. 8513 draws one on every metering core and the lead simply ends there, which is why this destination takes no riser.
stack._note: The device that used to arrive uninvited. It appears only when the intake row states a metering ratio.

_branch_note: The bus PT hangs on a shunt tap ABOVE the bus, so neither it nor its primary fuse ever lands in the main conductor path between the bus and the breaker. Stacks upward from bus_y; risers are generated between consecutive devices.

pinned.name: outgoing
pinned._y_note: The cable exit sits at the cubicle floor, so it is pinned rather than stacked -- a unit with fewer CTs must not raise its own cable termination. But a unit carrying all three CTs stacks past 9.034, so the pin gives way and the exit is pushed down to clear the last device by push_gap. Without that a third CT lands below its own cable termination.

_tie_note:
A bus tie is the one cubicle whose breaker does NOT hang off the bus -- it lies in the bus, in series, so the bus stops either side of it and the roles here draw what fills the space. That is also what splits the lineup into two buses: bus 1 ends at the tie's left connector and bus 2 starts at its right one, which falls out of the gap rather than needing to be stated. Off 8513's tie_horizontal, kept to its relative spacings; the dx values are shifted for our narrower left-hand margin and the breaker box is our own 0.777 rather than 8513's 0.9206, so the tie reads as the same breaker as every other cubicle's.

Elevations are 'dy' from the bus, the way the stack's are gaps from the device above -- there are no absolute numbers here to fall out of step with the sheet.

tie._bus_gaps_note: 0.062 outside each drawout connector, 8513's clearance. The whole tie sits 0.9 left of centre so that the 1.613 between its right connector and the end of the cubicle holds both CTs -- they are downstream of the breaker on the customer sheet, not one either side of it.
tie._text_note: The spec block sits inside the tie's own box. It carries five lines where an upright breaker carries four -- the tie states its normal position too -- so it starts higher than the 0.214 inset an upright box uses, or the last line lands on the box's bottom edge. A tie has no cable leaving the cubicle, so it has no destination to print.

devices.name: tie_breaker
devices._note: A plain box, not kind 'breaker'. That kind exists to interrupt the vertical conductor; this one interrupts the horizontal bus, and the interruption is declared in bus_gaps.

devices.name: tie_ct_mu
devices._attrib_note: HXF1CT prints its ratio right-aligned off its left edge, which on a cubicle this wide runs the label out into the neighbour. Moved into the clear space under the tie breaker instead. polarity_dot.dx is measured from the CUBICLE centreline, not from the symbol -- -0.518 is the CT's own polarity terminal. dy puts the mark on the bus at the same 0.05 stand-off the upright CTs use on their conductor; 8513 leaves it down at the secondary terminal, which reads as a junction dot floating clear of everything.
devices._note: The merging unit's own CT, nearer the breaker of the two on the bus-2 side. Its core is the differential one: it reaches the 87B relays through the process bus rather than through a run on this sheet.

devices.name: tie_ct
devices._attrib_note: Both CT labels are right-aligned on their own CT's right edge and sit on different rows. Side by side they would have run into each other; there is no room to stagger them left and right on this side of the cubicle.
devices._note: The tie relay's CT, the outer of the two. Tie current is the same through both, so which of the pair feeds which box is a matter of what routes without crossing.

devices.name: merging_unit
devices._note: Beside the tie relay, on the same row as every relay box in the lineup.

devices.name: relay_box
devices._note: At the lineup's relay elevation, not tucked under the tie breaker as 8513 does it. 8513's sheet is compressed around a mid-height bus; ours has room, and a row of relay boxes all on one line reads better than one of them floating up at the bus.

devices.name: tie_ct_mu_secondary
devices._note: Down, back along at 15.2 and into the merging unit at the far end of the cubicle. The along-leg passes 0.485 above the relay box rather than through it, and stops short of the other CT's drop, so the two secondaries never meet.

devices.name: tie_ct_secondary
devices._note: Straight down from the CT's left terminal into the tie relay below it.

tie._reference_dx_note: Where each voltage reference lands on the tie relay. The run for the tie's OWN bus arrives from behind it and stops at 0.9; the other arrives from ahead and starts at 1.75. Both rise into the same relay box, and the 0.85 between them is what stops the two runs reading as one line passing through.
tie._merging_unit_note: The merging unit digitises the tie's CT and publishes it to both differential relays over the process bus, which is why no copper differential run reaches the tie. It takes voltage from one bus only -- the tie's own -- where the relay beside it takes both.

relay_box._note: Outline around the relay label, which annotate_unit prints from the 'relay' column.

ct_compartment._note: Sized from the CTs actually present instead of from a remembered span. On a unit with a protection and a ground CT this yields 12.378..9.907, against the 12.465..9.912 drawn by hand on 8508 -- so the rule reproduces the reference without copying its number.

test_switch._note: Where the metering CT's secondary ends. Anchored to the CT's secondary terminal rather than to a sheet elevation, so it follows the CT down when the stack above it grows. Size and offset are 8513's.
test_switch._when_note: 'always' rather than 'ct_metering': what decides whether the switch is drawn is whether the anchor exists, and the anchor exists only because the metering CT declared a secondary that ends here. Naming the column again would be a second copy of that condition to keep in step.

conductor._note: The vertical run down the cubicle centreline. build_sld draws it between the series roles' gaps.

_decks_note: A two-high cubicle holds two breakers on one centreline, one row per deck, both rows carrying the same unit number. The upper deck is the lower deck reflected about the bus: same devices, same gaps, same symbols, running upward and taking its cable out through the roof. Reflecting rather than re-measuring is what makes the second deck free -- there is no second set of elevations to keep in step with the first.

upper._text_shift_note: MTEXT hangs downward from its insertion point, so reflecting the anchor alone would leave a four-line spec block growing out of the bottom of the breaker it belongs to. Each style is nudged up by roughly its own rendered height. These are the redline knobs -- adjust here if a label sits proud.
upper._hide_text_note: The unit number and tag describe the cubicle, and both decks share one. Printing them from each row stacks two headers at the same elevation. The upper deck's own tag and ratings still appear in its spec block beside its breaker.

_control_note: Lineup-wide horizontal runs. The bus PT's voltage reference is one of these, not a per-unit device: it originates at whichever unit states a 'pt' and drops into every unit that states a 'relay'. So it re-routes itself when the PT moves to a different cubicle, and it reaches exactly the units that have something to reference it.

buses.name: pt_reference
buses._end_dx_note: Must reach the LAST riser, not the last centreline. The risers drop at +1.336 (the relay box centre), so an end_dx of 0 leaves the final unit's drop hanging in mid-air just short of the run. start_dx stays 0 because the run originates under the PT cubicle's own centreline.
buses._reach_fuse_note: Every relay's supply is fused where it leaves the run -- 8513 draws one on each, and ours dropped unfused. half_height 0.1875 is the VFU1 body, so the break in the riser is the block's own size rather than a number to keep in step with it. 6A is 8513's rating, carried as the house default behind the 'relay_fuse' column.
buses._y_note: Below the relay boxes (bottom 14.043) and above the CT compartment (top 12.378), so it crosses neither. The riser at dx 1.336 is the relay box centreline, clear of the compartment's -1.081..0.290 span.
buses._note: A run needs two participants to be drawn, so a single-unit lineup, or one where only the PT cubicle carries a relay, correctly produces no run at all.
buses._source_dx_note: The PT secondary drops on its own offset, not the relay risers' 1.336 -- that line runs from the PT all the way down to the run and would pass straight through the source cubicle's own relay box. 2.1 clears the box's right edge at 1.925 and stays inside the cubicle, whose right edge is 2.313.
buses._per_bus_note: PTB1 and PTB2 are two references, not one. Drawn as a single run they met in the middle and read as one line straight through the tie -- which says every relay in the lineup sees the same voltage, and they do not. Each now stops at the tie, where the tie relay takes both.

buses.name: bus_differential
buses._per_bus_note: Declared once and built once per bus in the sheet, so a lineup with two buses gets 87B1 and 87B2 without a second entry here to keep in step with the first. Each cubicle feeds, and each relay terminates, the run belonging to its OWN bus -- which is what the customer sheet states: R-12 takes the five bus-1 cubicles, R-13 the five bus-2 ones, and the tie is in neither.
buses._y_note: In the only horizontal band that is clear the whole width of the lineup: above every CT compartment (top 12.378, fixed by the first CT's elevation) and below the PT reference run at 13.21. The obvious place -- down among the CTs, where 8508 draws its diff run at 10.255 -- works there because that run spans two adjacent cubicles. This one has to cross a dozen, and at CT elevation it would be drawn straight through every compartment box on the way.
buses._source_note: No 'reaches': the differential CTs put themselves on this run through their own secondaries, declared on the stack entry. What the run still needs is somewhere to end, and that is this -- the cubicle whose relay is the differential relay, named by the 'bus_differential' column. Move the relay to another cubicle and the run re-routes to it, exactly as the PT reference run follows the PT.
buses._zone_note: One run, so one differential zone. A lineup with a real two-zone scheme (87B1 and 87B2 either side of the tie) is two entries here with two columns behind them, not a change to the mechanism.

_ct_label_note: The ratio and class print BELOW the CT, which is the VXF1CT block's own attribute position and 8508's. 8513 pulls them out to the left instead, and that is not an improvement to copy here: 8513 draws no dashed CT compartment, so its labels sit in the space our box occupies. Asked for and settled -- leave them below.
_ct_class_note: A CT's ratio comes from its own column; its accuracy class comes from 'ct_class' if the unit row states one, and from the house default for that CT's job if it does not. One column rather than three because a cubicle's CTs almost always share a class -- a lineup that genuinely mixes them leaves it blank and takes the defaults.
